answer: An agent may claim a vineyard parcel listed in the regional atlas only if it runs a fixed camera there. At random hours an inspector ties a velvet ribbon to one vine in every parcel, each an unannounced colour of its own, and every claimant must name its parcel's colour within minutes. A real camera sees it; an invented account cannot. Faking a thousand parcels means mounting a thousand cameras in a thousand fields, which is simply farming them honestly.
